name: Lovable
product: AI app builder that turns plain-language prompts into working web apps and businesses.
lead_investors: Menlo Ventures; co-led by EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund
expansion_signal: Funding will expand platform, infrastructure and a global team, with hiring across Stockholm, London, Boston, San Francisco and New York.
africa_use_case: Nigerian, Kenyan and Ghanaian founders, freelancers and agencies could build client apps and MVPs without hiring developers, if they could pay the subscription in naira, shillings or cedis.
notes: $13.3B valuation; reported $400M+ ARR and 60M+ projects. Pricing tiers not confirmed in a source during this research.

name: Emergent
hq_country: India / United States (San Francisco and Bengaluru)
product: AI software creation (vibe coding) platform that lets non-technical founders and small businesses build full-stack web and mobile apps with autonomous agents.
lead_investors: Creaegis; co-leads Claypond Capital and Sentinel Global
africa_use_case: African SMB owners could build CRMs, inventory and marketplace apps for their own businesses instead of paying custom-dev agencies.
notes: $1.5B valuation; reported ~$120M run-rate and 200k+ paying customers; about 70% of users have no coding background.

name: Supabase
product: Open-source Postgres backend platform (database, auth, storage, functions) used by developers and AI app builders.
africa_use_case: African indie developers and startups who build on Supabase today often struggle to pay usage bills by card; local-currency funding would keep projects online.
notes: $10.5B post-money valuation. Website (supabase.com) not captured from a fetched source; verify.

name: Runpod
product: AI developer cloud offering GPU compute for training and running AI models.
round_stage: Growth (company blog calls it Series A)
expansion_signal: Capital earmarked for platform development, team growth and broader global access for its 1M+ developers.
africa_use_case: African ML engineers, researchers and AI startups need on-demand GPUs they cannot buy locally and would top up compute credits from a local-currency wallet.
notes: $1B valuation; founded by two former Comcast engineers (names not in sources seen).

name: Wispr (Wispr Flow)
product: AI voice dictation app for Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android that turns speech into clean text in any app, now adding a meeting notetaker.
pricing_model: Free tier; Pro about $15/month ($12/month billed annually)
lead_investors: Menlo Ventures; returning investor Notable Capital
expansion_signal: None stated (expansion is into new product areas such as meetings, not new geographies).
africa_use_case: Mobile-first African professionals, journalists and students could dictate emails and reports on Android phones, a strong fit for markets where phones dominate over laptops.
notes: $2B valuation. Pricing from third-party reviews (smartkeys.org, eesel.ai).

name: Otter.ai
product: AI meeting notetaker that transcribes, summarises and searches conversations.
expansion_signal: Company says the capital will fund enterprise growth, go-to-market, international expansion and product work; it already reports 40M+ users worldwide.
africa_use_case: African consultants, NGO staff, lecturers and students who sit in many Zoom/Teams calls would pay for transcripts and summaries, especially for English-language meetings.
notes: Financing is from GC's CVF, which funds marketing spend rather than taking equity; marketing-led growth plus explicit international expansion makes it a good pitch target.

name: Niteshift
product: Cloud platform that runs any frontier or open-source AI coding agent inside fully configured dev environments with live previews.
pricing_model: Free ($10 credits), Individual $50/month, Team $250/month, plus usage-based agent time
africa_use_case: African dev shops and remote freelancers working for foreign clients could run coding agents in the cloud instead of on weak local hardware and bandwidth.
notes: Pricing from rywalker.com research page (June 2026).

name: Lightsprint
product: Collaborative AI product-development platform where PMs, designers and business staff describe changes and coding agents ship pull requests on the existing codebase.
africa_use_case: Small African product teams with few engineers could let non-technical staff ship features directly.
notes: YC company; team-oriented product, likely priced per team. Round date taken from Business Insider publication date.

name: Runable
product: AI agent platform that builds websites and apps from prompts and then runs growth tasks such as ads, social media and AI-search visibility for small businesses.
lead_investors: Susquehanna Venture Capital, Nexus Venture Partners
expansion_signal: Reports 1.7M registered users with the US, UK and Japan as key markets, already selling well outside India.
africa_use_case: African micro-businesses (salons, caterers, boutiques) could get a website and run social and ad campaigns without an agency.
notes: $65M post-money. SMB focus and emerging-market origin make it a natural Africa pitch.

name: Maple
product: End-to-end encrypted private AI chat app plus a desktop AI agent (Maple Work), running models inside secure enclaves so the company cannot read user data.
pricing_model: Free tier; Pro $20/month; Max $100 and $200/month; Teams $30/user/month
expansion_signal: None stated (expanding into personal and enterprise agent products).
africa_use_case: African lawyers, journalists, health workers and activists handling sensitive data would pay for an AI assistant that cannot see their prompts.
founders: Mark Suman (CEO); co-founder surnamed Ronning (first name not in sources seen)
notes: Also uses maple.ai domain. Pricing from aibase.com and trymaple.ai/teams.

name: Instinct
product: Personal AI agent reachable by text and phone that connects to a user's apps and devices to organise their life and act on their behalf.
africa_use_case: Busy African professionals who already run their lives over SMS and WhatsApp-style messaging could delegate scheduling and errands to a text-based agent.
notes: Operated by Spear Street Technology. Invite-only beta at launch; earlier $250M Series B (Aug 26, 2026). Date 2026-09-28 per ZPlatform roundup; privacy scrutiny reported.

name: Fal
product: Generative media inference platform: one API to 1,500+ image, video, audio and 3D models, plus custom model hosting.
africa_use_case: African creative agencies, app developers and content creators building image/video features would buy API credits if they could fund them locally.
notes: $16B valuation. API-credit model suits wallet top-ups. Website (fal.ai) not captured from a fetched source; verify.

name: Modal
product: Serverless cloud for running AI models, inference, batch jobs and sandboxed code for developers.
africa_use_case: African AI startups and data scientists could deploy models without managing servers and pay per second of compute.
founders: Akshat Bubna (co-founder; others not in sources seen)
notes: $15.75B valuation; $1B+ annualized run rate; offices in New York, San Francisco and Stockholm.

name: Manus (Butterfly Effect)
product: General-purpose AI agent that produces slides, websites, games, video and designs from a plain-language request.
africa_use_case: African students, marketers and small-business owners could produce pitch decks, sites and research reports from one prompt.
notes: Chinese-founded, staff relocated to Singapore in 2025; Meta acquisition was unwound by Chinese regulators. Reported ~$4B valuation. Geopolitical/regulatory risk.

name: Cognition (Devin / Windsurf)
product: AI software engineering company behind the Devin coding agent and Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) AI code editor.
africa_use_case: Africa's large population of student and freelance developers would pay $20/month for an AI code editor if they could pay without a dollar card.
notes: $48B valuation. Pricing from dupple.com and devhunt.org (Nov 2026).

name: Factory
product: Agent-native software development platform whose 'Droids' automate coding, testing, code review and debugging.
lead_investors: Not found (backers include Blackstone, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia Capital)
africa_use_case: African software outsourcing firms serving foreign clients could use coding agents to deliver more work with small teams.
notes: $5B valuation; positioned for enterprise engineering teams, so self-serve fit is weaker.

name: Ploy
product: AI growth platform with autonomous agents that build, optimise and operate a company's website and marketing channels.
africa_use_case: African e-commerce sellers and service SMBs could replace an agency with agents that run their site, SEO and campaigns.
notes: Founder is Webflow co-founder/ex-CTO. Generally available to any user at launch.

name: Holo
product: AI marketing autopilot that plans and runs social and marketing content for small businesses.
expansion_signal: Reported 20,000+ paying customers across 100+ countries and $5M ARR; funding aims to reach more small businesses.
africa_use_case: African small businesses that sell mainly through Instagram, Facebook and TikTok would pay ~EUR 29/month for an AI social media manager.
founders: Deividas Kovger, Aleksandras Urbanavicius (from a community wiki; verify)
notes: Low price point and global self-serve base make it a strong Cozzipay pitch. Pricing and customer numbers from a Substack article.

name: Marker
product: AI-native word processor with a thesaurus, fact-checker and conversational editor that helps people write rather than writing for them.
africa_use_case: African students, academics and writers working in English could use it for essays, theses and articles.
notes: Co-founder is an ex-DeepMind creative lead; angels include Google Docs and Slack co-founders.

name: imagi
product: K-12 AI literacy and AI-assisted (vibe) coding curriculum with a FERPA/COPPA-compliant AI gateway for students and teachers.
expansion_signal: Funding to expand structured AI learning for students and teachers in the US and other international markets.
africa_use_case: African private schools, coding clubs and parents could buy AI and coding curricula to prepare children for tech careers.
notes: Partners with Lovable and OpenAI; backers include will.i.am. Sold mainly to schools, so payer may be institutions.

name: e2e (formerly TesterArmy)
hq_country: United States / Poland (San Francisco and Warsaw)
product: Open-source agentic end-to-end testing framework for web, iOS and Android apps that verifies code written by coding agents.
pricing_model: Free open-source framework; paid engineering help for rollouts
lead_investors: Not found (backers include Credo Ventures, KAYA, Point Nine)
africa_use_case: African mobile app teams shipping on Android could automate QA without hiring testers.
notes: YC company. Free core product means little to pay for today; weak payment fit.

name: Naïve
product: Infrastructure and unified API that lets AI agents set up and run a business end to end (incorporation, operations, day-to-day tasks).
africa_use_case: African solo founders and developers building agent-run online businesses could use it to automate back-office work.
notes: Palo Alto-based; 30,000+ developers within months of launch. Some business-setup features may be US-specific.

name: CloudBackend
product: AI cloud infrastructure that turns vibe-coded prototypes into production SaaS, bundling database, auth, subscriptions, payments, CRM, support and analytics.
expansion_signal: None stated (funding to broaden platform access and integrations with AI coding tools).
africa_use_case: African creators turning AI-built apps into paid SaaS need subscriptions and payments; Cozzipay could be both a payment method for CloudBackend and an option inside its payments module.
notes: Linkoping-based. Built-in payments module suggests a partnership angle beyond pay-in.

name: fonio.ai
product: AI phone and omnichannel assistant that answers and automates customer calls for small and medium-sized businesses.
expansion_signal: Funding to bring its AI customer-communication tools to SMBs across Europe and the United States.
africa_use_case: African clinics, restaurants and service businesses that lose customers to missed calls could use an AI receptionist in English or French.
notes: $140M valuation; company says it passed $10M ARR within 12 months. Press page fetched but no email visible.

name: LangChain
product: Open-source frameworks and the LangSmith platform for building, observing and running AI agents.
africa_use_case: African developers and AI startups already using the open-source LangChain libraries could upgrade to paid LangSmith seats for tracing and deployment.
notes: $3B valuation; message focuses on businesses owning their agents, so enterprise tilt.

name: Well
product: AI assistant aimed at small-business founders to handle their admin and business tasks.
africa_use_case: Francophone African small-business founders (Senegal, Cote d'Ivoire, Cameroon) could use a French-built AI assistant for business admin.
notes: Based at Station F, Paris; founders ex-Qonto and Fintecture. Francophone angle is useful for West/Central Africa.

name: Catch
product: Agentic AI admin assistant for business leaders that handles scheduling, email, travel, follow-ups and outbound calls.
africa_use_case: African founders and executives who cannot afford a full-time assistant could delegate calendar and email admin.
notes: Tel Aviv-based; executive focus may mean higher price point.

name: Orbits (Bit)
hq_country: Canada / United States (Toronto and San Francisco)
product: Bit, an AI household assistant app for iOS and Android that manages family calendars, groceries, home maintenance and errands.
africa_use_case: Urban middle-class African families could use it to coordinate school runs, shopping and household staff.
founders: Erik Tillberg (co-founder and CTO; others not in sources seen)
notes: Consumer product; many integrations likely North America-centric.

name: Klarent
product: Autonomous software testing platform where AI agents write and maintain deterministic test code for web and mobile apps.
pricing_model: Not found (self-serve option and fully managed service both offered)
expansion_signal: Funding pays for a move into the United States and sales hiring in the US and UK.
africa_use_case: African fintech and app teams could outsource QA to AI agents rather than build testing teams.
notes: Formerly fore ai. Product described as built for enterprise; self-serve tier mentioned by saasworthy.com.

name: Mistlabs (Ambi)
product: Ambi, an ambient AI assistant app for iPhone, Mac and Apple Watch that listens in the background and offers real-time help and notes.
africa_use_case: African professionals on Apple devices could capture meetings and conversations automatically; reach limited by low iPhone share.
notes: Funding also targets a future standalone wearable (hardware). Apple-only today, which limits Africa reach.

name: Town
product: Personalised AI work assistant that learns how a person works across email, calendar, messages and work apps, now extended to whole teams.
africa_use_case: African consultants and small professional-services firms could delegate inbox and scheduling work to an assistant.
notes: $1B valuation; also raised a $55M Series A on 2026-06-03 (a16z). Pricing from eesel.ai review.

name: Fish Audio
product: AI voice platform for expressive real-time text-to-speech, voice cloning and voice agents, with open-weight models and a paid hosted API.
pricing_model: Free open models; paid hosted API/app usage (exact rates not found)
africa_use_case: African YouTubers, podcasters, ed-tech builders and call-centre startups could generate voiceovers and voice agents at lower cost than incumbents.
founders: Shijia Liao (co-founder and chief scientist; others not in sources seen)
notes: Reported $21M ARR and 8M users in first year. Voice-cloning misuse concerns noted by Tech Times.
